explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates LLM-as-judge (GPT-4o) against human annotations on a random sample of 100 outputs, reporting percentage agreement metrics for both answerability and correctness

prompts.notes: Full prompt provided in Appendix A.6; uses binary evaluation format checking answerability and correctness against reference answers

guidelines.notes: Human annotators evaluate binary answerability and correctness of question-answer pairs from summaries, but detailed guidelines not explicitly described

sample_size.notes: 100 outputs randomly sampled, equally split between answerable and non-answerable cases; 3 human annotations per sample

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-4o as judge shows high agreement with human annotations (86.4% for answerability, 95.3% for correctness), demonstrating reliability of automatic evaluation method.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM and human evaluate identical criteria (answerability and correctness) on the same question-answer pairs
